title: Elements of art
examples: Can you point out the line in this drawing?
What is the difference between shape and form?
How does colour affect a painting's mood?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the elements of art.

draw.text: Elements of Art: Line, Shape, Form

explain.say: Line is a mark made by a moving point.
A shape is a two dimensional area enclosed by lines.
Form is a three dimensional object you can see around you.
Colour refers to the property of light reflected off a surface.
Texture describes how a surface feels or appears to feel.

faq.q: What is the difference between shape and form?
faq.a: A shape is flat, like drawing on paper. A form has depth, like a real ball.

faq.q: Does value only mean black and white?
faq.a: No, value is about how light or dark a colour is. It ranges from the lightest to the darkest.
Space refers to the area around, between, or within objects in a work of art.
asks: Do I need to worry about space?

faq.q: Can texture be real or just look real?
faq.a: Yes, texture can be actual, like touching bark. It can also be implied, like painting to look rough.

faq.q: Are all colours considered elements of art?
faq.a: Colour is one element, but it interacts with others like line and value. It is a key component.
asks: Is colour the most important element?
How does colour relate to light?

facts: Line can suggest movement or direction in a piece.
A shape is defined by its boundaries, making it two dimensional.
Form gives the illusion of three dimensions, like a sculpture.
Value describes the lightness or darkness of a colour or tone.

quiz.say: Which element describes the flatness of an object?
quiz.why: Shape is specifically defined as a two dimensional area, meaning it has length and width but no depth.

wrong.0: Line is just a path, it does not enclose an area to create a shape.
wrong.1: Space is the area around the object, not the object itself.
wrong.3: Form is three dimensional, so it includes depth, which is more than just flat.

quiz.say: If you are painting a ball, which element are you trying to show?
quiz.why: Because a ball takes up space in three dimensions, showing height, width, and depth, you are representing form.

wrong.0: Colour is just one quality of the ball, not the overall three-dimensional quality.
wrong.1: Texture describes how the ball feels, not its actual three-dimensional structure.
wrong.3: Shape would only show the outline of the ball as if it were flat on paper.

quiz.say: Which element is best shown by the contrast between a dark shadow and a bright highlight?
quiz.why: The difference between light and dark is the definition of value, which helps create the illusion of form.

wrong.1: Colour is about the hue, while value is about the brightness of that hue.
wrong.2: Line can create value, but the overall contrast between light and dark is the element of value.
wrong.3: Shape only concerns the outline, not the tonal difference within the shape.
